definitions.acs_sample: ACS 2013 5-year PUMS (data years 2009-13), ages 25-34, SCHL >= 12, armed forces and unemployed with 15+ usual hours dropped, group quarters in (acs_occupations.build_sample, rules='workbook'); each person has total weight 1 split between the reported occupation (u = 1, or 0.5 for 15-29 usual hours) and home production
definitions.ba: ACS: SCHL >= 21 (bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate); graduate: SCHL >= 22; BA only: SCHL == 21. NLSY79: highest grade completed >= 16 at some round at 25-34

definitions.years_of_schooling: HHJK highgrade from SCHL (grade 9 = 9, diploma/GED 12, some college 13, associate 14, bachelor 16, graduate 19) bounded to [9, 17]
definitions.wage_sample: employed, 30+ usual hours, 48+ weeks, wage and business income >= $1,000 in 2010 dollars; log hourly wage in 1999 dollars (workbook rules)

conventions.P: population weights: every (person, cell) row weighted by PWGTP x u
conventions.T2: occupation x gender cell means weighted by PWGTP x u, combined with the unweighted Table 2 counts (sums of u) of the population in question; SEs hold the counts fixed
conventions.wsw: cell means combined with wage-sample record counts
conventions.PW: cell means combined with PWGTP-weighted counts
conventions.age: PWGTP-weighted regression with single-year age dummies (and a female dummy when pooled); age_occupation adds gender x occupation fixed effects

nces_salary.title: Digest of Education Statistics 2022, Table 211.20
nces_salary.notes:
NOTE: This table includes regular full-time teachers only; it excludes other staff even when they have full-time teaching duties (regular part-time teachers, itinerant teachers, long-term substitutes, administrators, library media specialists, other professional staff, and support staff). Teachers were asked how many school years they had worked as a teacher. In 2011-12 and earlier years, teachers were also asked how many of their teaching years were full time and how many were part time. After 2011-12, teachers were no longer asked how many years were full time versus part time. Throughout this table, all school years are counted, regardless of whether teachers taught full time or part time. Some data have been revised from previously published figures. Detail may not sum to totals because of rounding.
SOURCE: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics, Schools and Staffing Survey (SASS), "Public School Teacher Data File," 1990-91, 1999-2000, 2007-08, and 2011-12; and "Charter School Teacher Data File," 1999-2000; and National Teacher and Principal Survey (NTPS), "Public School Teacher Data File," 2015-16, 2017-18, and 2020-21. (This table was prepared September 2022.)

tuition.notes_330_10:
NOTE: Data are for the entire academic year and are average charges for full-time students. Tuition and fees were weighted by the number of full-time-equivalent undergraduates, but were not adjusted to reflect student residency. Room and board are based on full-time students. Data through 1995-96 are for institutions of higher education, while later data are for degree-granting institutions. Degree-granting institutions grant associate’s or higher degrees and participate in Title IV federal financial aid programs. The degree-granting classification is very similar to the earlier higher education classification, but it includes more 2-year colleges and excludes a few higher education institutions that did not grant degrees. Some data have been revised from previously published figures. Detail may not sum to totals because of rounding.
SOURCE: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics, Projections of Education Statistics to 1986-87; Higher Education General Information Survey (HEGIS), "Institutional Characteristics of Colleges and Universities" surveys, 1969-70 through 1985-86; "Fall Enrollment in Institutions of Higher Education" surveys, 1963 through 1985; Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), "Fall Enrollment Survey" (IPEDS-EF:86-99) and "Institutional Characteristics Survey" (IPEDS-IC:86-99); IPEDS Spring 2001 through Spring 2018, Fall Enrollment component; and IPEDS Fall 2000 through Fall 2017, Institutional Characteristics component. (This table was prepared November 2018.)
tuition.notes_331_30:
NOTE: Excludes students who previously attended another postsecondary institution or who began their studies on a part-time basis. Includes only first-time, full-time students who paid the in-state or in-district tuition rate (if they attended public institutions) and who were awarded Title IV aid. Excludes the approximately 17 percent of students who were not awarded any Title IV aid. Title IV aid includes grant aid, work-study aid, and loan aid. Data are weighted by the number of students at the institution who were awarded Title IV aid. Totals include students for whom income data were not available. Some data have been revised from previously published figures.
SOURCE: U.S. Department of Education, National Center for Education Statistics, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), Spring 2011 and Winter 2016-17 through Winter 2018-19, Student Financial Aid component. (This table was prepared December 2019.)

ba_share_nonteacher.scale_rule: 5% of the value (modelling tolerance; the sampling SE is far smaller)
ba_share_nonteacher.n_universe_note: Table 2 person-equivalents of non-teachers (home production included)
ba_share_nonteacher.definition: share with a bachelor's degree or more (SCHL >= 21) among non-teachers aged 25-34, men and women pooled; non-teachers = every non-K-12-teaching occupation plus home production (Table 2 universe); cell shares weighted by PWGTP, combined with the Table 2 counts
ba_share_nonteacher.model: share of adults with d = 1 among non-teachers (all non-teaching occupations and home production)

ba_premium.definition: mean log hourly wage of non-teacher market workers with a BA or more minus those without, men and women pooled, full-time full-year wage sample; occupation x gender cell means (PWGTP) weighted by the Table 2 counts of each education group (raw: no occupation control)
ba_premium.model: mean log wage of d = 1 minus d = 0 among non-teacher market workers (home production out), cells weighted by the model's shares; the model's non-teaching occupation choice does not depend on d, so this equals its within-occupation premium
ba_premium.tradeoff: Alternative forms of ONE moment (choice_group ba_premium): use one of them in a criterion. ba_premium (raw) is the total return to a BA, including the BA holders' sorting into better-paid occupations, which the model's non-teaching occupation choice (independent of d) cannot generate, so rho_c would absorb it; ba_premium_within_occupation is the premium within occupation, which is the model's premium by construction, but it leaves the model's total return to college below the data's. Which one is primary is the M3 designer's choice.

ba_premium_within_occupation.definition: coefficient on BA+ in a PWGTP-weighted regression of log hourly wage on BA+, single-year age dummies and occupation x gender fixed effects, non-teacher market workers, men and women pooled: the BA premium within occupation
ba_premium_within_occupation.model: ba_premium when occupation cells are held fixed: the model has one credential premium rho_c in every non-teaching occupation and no BA-specific occupational sorting, so this is its counterpart of rho_c plus selection on z
ba_premium_within_occupation.tradeoff: Alternative forms of ONE moment (choice_group ba_premium): use one of them in a criterion. ba_premium (raw) is the total return to a BA, including the BA holders' sorting into better-paid occupations, which the model's non-teaching occupation choice (independent of d) cannot generate, so rho_c would absorb it; ba_premium_within_occupation is the premium within occupation, which is the model's premium by construction, but it leaves the model's total return to college below the data's. teacher_premium_core_all.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers of the core codes 2310-2330 (96% BA+) minus that of all non-teacher market workers (cell means weighted by Table 2 counts), men and women pooled; pooled = average of the two with the K-12 wage-sample weights 0.2444/0.7556
teacher_premium_core_all.model: teachers of the licensure codes against all non-teachers

teacher_premium_core_all_m.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers of the core codes 2310-2330 (96% BA+) minus that of all non-teacher market workers (cell means weighted by Table 2 counts), men
teacher_premium_core_all_m.model: teachers of the licensure codes against all non-teachers

teacher_premium_core_all_f.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers of the core codes 2310-2330 (96% BA+) minus that of all non-teacher market workers (cell means weighted by Table 2 counts), women
teacher_premium_core_all_f.model: teachers of the licensure codes against all non-teachers

teacher_premium_core_ba.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers of the core codes 2310-2330 (96% BA+) minus that of non-teacher market workers with a BA or more (cell means weighted by the Table 2 counts of the BA+ workers), men and women pooled; pooled = average of the two with the K-12 wage-sample weights 0.2444/0.7556
teacher_premium_core_ba.model: teachers of the licensure codes against d = 1 non-teachers

teacher_premium_core_ba_m.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers of the core codes 2310-2330 (96% BA+) minus that of non-teacher market workers with a BA or more (cell means weighted by the Table 2 counts of the BA+ workers), men
teacher_premium_core_ba_m.model: teachers of the licensure codes against d = 1 non-teachers

teacher_premium_core_ba_f.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers of the core codes 2310-2330 (96% BA+) minus that of non-teacher market workers with a BA or more (cell means weighted by the Table 2 counts of the BA+ workers), women
teacher_premium_core_ba_f.model: teachers of the licensure codes against d = 1 non-teachers

teacher_ba_wage_gap.model_moment: none (pay penalty of a non-BA teaching track)
teacher_ba_wage_gap.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers with a BA or more minus those without (pre-K/K and other instructors, mostly), men and women pooled, wage sample
teacher_ba_wage_gap.model: mean log wage of d = 1 teachers minus d = 0 teachers when the model has a non-BA teaching track (its pay penalty, rho_T0, in the model's terms)

teacher_ba_wage_gap_m.model_moment: none (pay penalty of a non-BA teaching track)
teacher_ba_wage_gap_m.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers with a BA or more minus those without (pre-K/K and other instructors, mostly), men, wage sample
teacher_ba_wage_gap_m.model: mean log wage of d = 1 teachers minus d = 0 teachers when the model has a non-BA teaching track (its pay penalty, rho_T0, in the model's terms)

teacher_ba_wage_gap_f.model_moment: none (pay penalty of a non-BA teaching track)
teacher_ba_wage_gap_f.definition: mean log hourly wage of K-12 teachers with a BA or more minus those without (pre-K/K and other instructors, mostly), women, wage sample
teacher_ba_wage_gap_f.model: mean log wage of d = 1 teachers minus d = 0 teachers when the model has a non-BA teaching track (its pay penalty, rho_T0, in the model's terms)

grad_teacher_premium.definition: log hourly wage of K-12 teachers with a graduate degree minus teachers with exactly a bachelor's degree, controlling for single-year age (and sex)
grad_teacher_premium.model: none (no graduate margin); compare with the salary-schedule premium

ma_ba_salary_premium.convention: delta method, experience rows weighted by the number of teachers
ma_ba_salary_premium.definition: log of the average base salary of full-time public school teachers with a master's degree over that with a bachelor's degree, 1-5 years of teaching experience
ma_ba_salary_premium.model: theta_s x log(17.5/16) (the schedule premium implied by the credential-lane elasticity); no graduate margin otherwise

teacher_z_gap_employed_nonteachers.definition: mean latent AFQT of K-12 teachers minus that of employed non-teachers (comparison A), employed sample, 1980 Census codes, majority-of-rounds rule
teacher_z_gap_employed_nonteachers.model: teacher_z_gap_market_sd (mean log z of teachers minus non-teacher workers over s_z)

teacher_z_gap_nonteacher_ba.definition: mean latent AFQT of K-12 teachers minus that of non-teacher persons with 16+ years (comparison B), employed sample, 1980 Census codes, majority-of-rounds rule
teacher_z_gap_nonteacher_ba.model: teacher z gap against / within BA+ (needs d)

teacher_z_gap_within_ba.definition: mean latent AFQT of K-12 teachers minus that of non-teachers with 16+ years, teachers with 16+ years only (comparison C), employed sample, 1980 Census codes, majority-of-rounds rule
teacher_z_gap_within_ba.model: teacher z gap against / within BA+ (needs d)

p_ba_afqt_tercile_1.definition: share with 16+ years of schooling in tercile 1 of own OBSERVED AFQT (terciles of the weighted sample of persons observed at 25-34, highest grade >= 9; cut points -0.403, 0.494 observed SDs), at the NLSY79 BA share (0.258, against 0.339 in the ACS)
p_ba_afqt_tercile_1.model: P(d = 1 | tercile) of a NOISY score x = sqrt(R) theta + sqrt(1 - R) u with theta = standardized log z, u standard normal, R = 0.916 (terciles of x over adults); for a noise-free model use alt_latent_scale (terciles of log z itself)
p_ba_afqt_tercile_1.alt_note: alt_at_acs_share: the observed-score logit with its level shifted to the ACS BA share; alt_latent_scale: terciles of the latent factor from the errors-in-variables logit (assumes a normal latent factor and a logistic P(BA | theta)); *_at_acs_share: level shifted to the ACS BA share

p_ba_afqt_tercile_2.definition: share with 16+ years of schooling in tercile 2 of own OBSERVED AFQT (terciles of the weighted sample of persons observed at 25-34, highest grade >= 9; cut points -0.403, 0.494 observed SDs), at the NLSY79 BA share (0.258, against 0.339 in the ACS)
p_ba_afqt_tercile_2.model: P(d = 1 | tercile) of a NOISY score x = sqrt(R) theta + sqrt(1 - R) u with theta = standardized log z, u standard normal, R = 0.916 (terciles of x over adults); for a noise-free model use alt_latent_scale (terciles of log z itself)
p_ba_afqt_tercile_2.alt_note: alt_at_acs_share: the observed-score logit with its level shifted to the ACS BA share; alt_latent_scale: terciles of the latent factor from the errors-in-variables logit (assumes a normal latent factor and a logistic P(BA | theta)); *_at_acs_share: level shifted to the ACS BA share

p_ba_afqt_tercile_3.definition: share with 16+ years of schooling in tercile 3 of own OBSERVED AFQT (terciles of the weighted sample of persons observed at 25-34, highest grade >= 9; cut points -0.403, 0.494 observed SDs), at the NLSY79 BA share (0.258, against 0.339 in the ACS)
p_ba_afqt_tercile_3.model: P(d = 1 | tercile) of a NOISY score x = sqrt(R) theta + sqrt(1 - R) u with theta = standardized log z, u standard normal, R = 0.916 (terciles of x over adults); for a noise-free model use alt_latent_scale (terciles of log z itself)
p_ba_afqt_tercile_3.alt_note: alt_at_acs_share: the observed-score logit with its level shifted to the ACS BA share; alt_latent_scale: terciles of the latent factor from the errors-in-variables logit (assumes a normal latent factor and a logistic P(BA | theta)); *_at_acs_share: level shifted to the ACS BA share

p_ba_afqt_top_minus_bottom.definition: top minus bottom AFQT tercile, share with 16+ years of schooling

afqt_logit_slope.definition: slope of the logit of P(16+ years of schooling) on observed AFQT (standardized)
afqt_logit_slope.model: slope of logit P(d = 1) on the NOISY score x = sqrt(R) theta + sqrt(1 - R) u (theta = log z standardized, u standard normal, R = 0.916); the observed score is attenuated, so a noise-free model needs afqt_logit_slope_latent instead

afqt_logit_slope_latent.definition: slope of the logit of P(16+ years of schooling) on the latent AFQT factor (SD units), by maximum likelihood with a normal latent factor and the composite reliability R = 0.916 (Gauss-Hermite integration over the factor given the score); the first-order correction slope_obs / sqrt(R) understates it
afqt_logit_slope_latent.model: d logit P(d = 1 | z) / d (log z / s_z): the slope of the logit of the model's BA probability on standardized log z (weighted over adults)

tuition_Fc.units: units of Cbar = mean annual expenditures per ADULT ($32,223 = CE $61,224 / 1.9 adults per consumer unit)
tuition_Fc.convention: (ii-a) total BA cost over 40 years of consumption per adult, undiscounted
tuition_Fc.definition: central: net tuition and fees (after grants and education tax benefits), public and private nonprofit 4-year weighted by undergraduate enrollment, 4 years, over 40 years of annual consumption per adult: the undiscounted, per-person counterpart of a one-off goods cost paid from adult consumption in a model without an interest rate whose other education parameters are calibrated on annual aggregate flows
tuition_Fc.model: Fc, goods cost of a BA in Node.m (and Xi), common to all college goers
tuition_Fc.per_cu_note: per consumer unit (the first release of this file) understates a per-person cost by the number of adults per unit, 1.9
tuition_Fc.range_note: per adult; low = net tuition and fees at public 4-year, 4 years, undiscounted; high = published tuition and fees, all 4-year, discounted at 3%
